scope: Source-context and physical row-to-item/field reconciliation only for the UA original 1985 printed p.26 Weight and Damage by Weapon Type table and Armor Class Table. No catalog, authored equipment, citation override, source table contract, or shared ledger mutation is made by this proposal.

source.title: Unearthed Arcana
source.visualVerification: I compared the authorized original source PDF render to the full table excerpts and inspected full-page row-focus overlays. Overlay rectangles for each of the 68 weight/damage rows include the complete printed row label, weight cell, both damage cells, and any visible row marker. The 11 Armor Class focus rectangles include the complete logical line, all wrapped continuation lines, and rating. This is geometry review against the source image, not an independent transcription audit beyond the frozen source-first manifest.
source.privateSourcePolicy: The original PDF and full-page renders remain outside the public repository. Only the limited p.27 note-block crop named below was added as a proposed continuation excerpt.

weightDamageRowTargetCounts.explanation: Row dispositions and target edges use different denominators: the combined Blowgun and needle row has a confirmed combined-item target plus a separate uncertain generic-blowgun candidate; Aklys is the one uncertain-only row. Jo Stick and hand quarrel have no target.

excludedCandidateEdgesFromRowLabelMismat.reason: The frozen candidate list includes a shield item, but this Armor Class line has no shield token and names only unshielded armor alternatives. Do not treat the candidate or its catalog excerpts as source-row evidence.

armorClassRowTargetCounts.note: A source row’s AC rating belongs to its entire printed line/alternatives. Shield candidates and elfin-chain variants stay uncertain where indicated.

fieldInventory.comparisonLimit: The 48 p.26 field values match the frozen manifest source cells after typographic dash/space and gp-weight normalization. That join does not automatically promote other-book base fields, assert target scope, or imply field-citation approvals.

legacyCatalogInventory.note: Catalog region identifiers are assessed per target-catalog occurrence because some legacy IDs resolve to different image filenames/hashes in different item catalogs. A matching label crop still lacks complete table context unless it points to the complete table image.

focusReview.fitMethod: Overlay focus geometry is defined in local pixels of each existing complete table crop, then transformed via the frozen region normalizedPageRect to source page coordinates. Weight table rows use the visually checked 19-pixel line pitch; Armor Class foci group the 2-line wrapped alternatives into one complete logical row. Each overlay was visually checked against the original p.26 PDF render and corresponding crop.

weightDamageTable.sourceCropEvidence: Frozen catalog occurrence for the complete Weight and Damage by Weapon Type table; inspected against original PDF page 27. It contains heading, all column labels and rows, the full gold-piece weight unit, and the facing-page note cue.

armorClassTable.sourceCropEvidence: Frozen catalog crop includes the ARMOR CLASS TABLE title, Type of Armor and Armor Class Rating headers, all 11 logical rows, complete wrap lines, and numeric ratings; visually checked against original PDF page 27.

facingPageNotes.sourceCropEvidence: Limited excerpt contains all eight marked note lines plus the complete two-line General Note. No page margin or unrelated page material was included. Original page-28 full render remains private.

noteCropRows.printedText: ** These weapons do twice the damage indicated to size L creatures when set (firmly grounded) to receive a charging opponent.
** These weapons are capable of dismounting a rider on a score equal to or greater than the “to hit” score.
1 These weapons do twice the indicated damage against creatures of any size when employed by an attacker riding a charging mount.
2 This weapon does twice the damage indicated to any opponent when the weapon is set to receive their charge.
3 This weapon class includes all pointed cutting and thrusting weapons with blade length between 15 and 24 inches.
4 These weapons are capable of disarming an opponent on a score required to hit AC 8.
5 Treat this weapon as a long sword if it is used one-handed.
6 Minor variations of these weapons, with different names, may exist in the campaign. See Players Handbook for particulars.
General Note: Any weapon strikes at +2 “to hit” against an opponent’s back (or similarly unseen); against stunned, prone, and motionless opponents, any weapon strikes at +4 “to hit.”
noteCropRows.appliesTo: all weapon rows; general +2 to-hit from back/similarly unseen and +4 to-hit versus stunned, prone, motionless opponents

semanticConstraints: “Approximate Weight in Gold Pieces” is mass/encumbrance, not purchase price. The row’s gp-weight must never be represented as a price.
Aklys is unqualified in the p.26 table while the current item is specifically Aklys (hurled); retain uncertain scope rather than assuming it covers every Aklys variant.
Blowgun and needle is one combined source row. Do not attribute the row cells to Blowgun alone; that candidate remains uncertain.
Jo Stick and Quarrel (or Bolt), hand have no confirmed equipment owners in the frozen source-first target set. Do not remap Jo Stick to the distinct Bo Stick row or hand quarrel to hand crossbow.
Light-, medium-, and heavy-horse lances are separate source rows with distinct weights and damage. Preserve all three IDs and horse qualifiers; do not collapse them into one generic lance value.
Armor Class row ratings describe the complete printed alternatives/configurations. Do not write a shielded/composite line rating into a generic Armor class without shield field.
Shield only is an unspecified shield type; the large shield, small shield, small wooden shield and buckler candidates remain uncertain.
Elfin chain mail is a distinct named variant in two Armor Class lines. Similarity to ordinary chain mail is not proof of equivalence.
Facing-page note assignments are made only for clearly transcribed markers. Glaive, Guisarme and Guisarme-Voulge markers remain unresolved; do not infer note numbers for them.
